stories.title: ‘Don’t shoot. Listen’: The AI-aided quest to understand Yellowstone’s wolves
stories.summary: Jeff Reed grew up believing you shoot wolves on sight. Then one night on his Montana farm, a gray wolf stood 10 yards from his truck and just looked at him. He fired over its back instead — and that moment turned him into a collaborator on the Cry Wolf Project, using AI and bioacoustics to decode wolf howls in Yellowstone.
stories.extended_summary: The wolf stood broadside in Jeff Reed's headlights, 10 yards away, and didn't move. Reed grabbed his rifle, aimed — and then something cracked open. "What the hell am I doing? Why am I doing this?" He shot over its back. The wolf didn't bolt. It just trotted alongside him and kept going. That night turned a lifelong wolf-hater into an unlikely ally of the world's longest-running wolf research effort. Reed, a Ph.D. linguist who spent years leading software engineering in Silicon Valley, now helps power the Cry Wolf Project — a Yellowstone-based effort using artificial intelligence and bioacoustics to understand what wolves are actually saying to each other. He calls that night his Apostle Paul moment. The wolf, it turns out, was talking. Reed just had to learn how to listen.
